title: Read and write numbers to 1 000 000 in standard, expanded and word form

lesson.title: Big Numbers: Up to One Million!

steps.say: You already know how to read and write numbers up to ten thousand, like six thousand four hundred and five. Today we take one big step further, all the way up to one million, and the neat part is that nothing new really happens. The places just keep going.

Here is the big idea. Every time you move one place to the left, the value gets ten times bigger. Ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, then ten thousands, then hundred thousands, and finally one million. Think of it like BC Place stadium. It holds about fifty four thousand people. That five is not just a five, it is five ten thousands, which is fifty thousand people.

visual.caption: 54 000 — the 5 sits in the ten thousands place

steps.say: Let's read a real number together. The city of Surrey has about six hundred eighteen thousand four hundred and thirty people. In standard form we write it with a little space instead of a comma, like this: six one eight, space, four three zero. Notice the space splits it into two chunks. The chunk on the left, six hundred eighteen, tells you the thousands. So you just read that chunk, say the word thousand, then read the rest.

visual.caption: 618 430 — read the left chunk, say “thousand”, then the rest

steps.say: Now expanded form. Expanded form just means writing what each digit is really worth, and adding them up. The six is worth six hundred thousand. The one is worth ten thousand. The eight is worth eight thousand. The four is worth four hundred. The three is worth thirty. And the zero is worth nothing, so we leave it out. Add all those pieces and you get right back to six hundred eighteen thousand four hundred and thirty.

Here is a mistake lots of kids make. Someone hears three hundred five thousand and writes three five zero zero zero, which is only thirty five thousand. Oops, that is way too small! Remember, the thousands chunk needs all three spots filled. Three hundred five is three, zero, five. So the answer is three zero five, space, zero zero zero. Those zeros are not nothing, they are place holders doing an important job.
So here is the whole trick. Find the space, read the left chunk and say thousand, then read the right chunk. And in expanded form, every digit gets to say what it is truly worth.

lesson.answer: Read big numbers in chunks: say the part before the space, add “thousand”, then say the rest — and in expanded form each digit shows its true value.

practice.question: A new community centre in Kelowna cost two hundred forty seven thousand and sixty dollars. Write that amount in standard form, then write it in expanded form.
practice.answer: Standard form: 247 060 dollars. Expanded form: 200 000 + 40 000 + 7 000 + 60. (The hundreds place is a zero, so it has no piece of its own — but the zero must still be written to hold its spot.)
